project.name: open-quake
project.description: Open driver + multi-grid touchscreen launcher for the DK-QUAKE / ARIS-68 touchscreen-and-knob macro device. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

nodes.name: actionRunner.js
nodes.summary: Executes launcher actions by resolving application paths, starting programs or shell commands, and locking the Windows workstation.

nodes.name: resolveAppPath
nodes.summary: Resolves an application identifier to an executable path using direct paths or platform command lookup.

nodes.name: launchApp
nodes.summary: Launches a resolved executable or delegates a path to the desktop shell while recording failures.

nodes.name: lockWorkstation
nodes.summary: Locks the active workstation using the platform-appropriate system command.

nodes.name: ahk.js
nodes.summary: Locates AutoHotkey and runs either script files or generated temporary scripts for programmable desktop automation.

nodes.name: findAhkExe
nodes.summary: Searches configured, installed, and PATH locations for an AutoHotkey executable and caches the result.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Runs an AutoHotkey file or materializes inline script text into a temporary file before spawning it.

nodes.name: desktopFocus.js

nodes.name: runPs
nodes.summary: Executes a PowerShell query with timeout and normalized output handling.

nodes.name: listRunningApps
nodes.summary: Enumerates and deduplicates visible Windows applications, returning a consistently sorted list.

nodes.name: tick
nodes.summary: Samples the foreground process with debouncing and notifies listeners after a stable focus change.

nodes.name: haClient.js
nodes.summary: Connects to Home Assistant over WebSocket and HTTP to retrieve registries, synthesize entity metadata, and fetch entity state.

nodes.name: withWebSocket

nodes.name: fetchAll
nodes.summary: Fetches all relevant Home Assistant registries in one authenticated WebSocket workflow and returns a normalized snapshot.

nodes.name: fetchEntityState
nodes.summary: Retrieves the current state of one Home Assistant entity through its REST endpoint.

nodes.name: mediaKeys.js
nodes.summary: Provides a Windows media-key controller that sends playback and volume commands through a reusable helper process.

nodes.name: createMediaKeys
nodes.summary: Creates a stateful media-key adapter that manages command dispatch, helper lifecycle, and cleanup.

nodes.name: meetingControl.js
nodes.summary: Controls meeting actions in Microsoft Teams and Zoom by focusing application windows and sending keyboard shortcuts.

nodes.name: focusTeamsWindow
nodes.summary: Finds and focuses a Microsoft Teams meeting window before automation commands are sent.

nodes.name: multiKnob.js
nodes.summary: Adapts the native multi-knob device driver into a stable JavaScript interface for screen, lighting, microphone, buzzer, firmware, and DFU controls.

nodes.name: MultiKnob

nodes.name: touchSetup.js

nodes.name: enumDisplays

nodes.name: runElevatedScript
nodes.summary: Writes and launches a temporary PowerShell script with elevation, then coordinates completion and cleanup.

nodes.name: clearAllCalibrations
nodes.summary: Clears persisted touchscreen calibration data through an elevated Windows operation.

nodes.name: haschedule.js
nodes.summary: Polls Home Assistant calendar and agenda data, normalizes events, and maintains a sorted schedule snapshot for the dashboard.

nodes.name: eventSortKey
nodes.summary: Derives a stable chronological sort key from heterogeneous event date and time fields.

nodes.name: poll
nodes.summary: Fetches current Home Assistant schedule data and updates the cached agenda and event snapshot.

nodes.name: lyrics.js
nodes.summary: Fetches, parses, caches, and exposes synchronized lyrics for the currently playing track.

nodes.name: parseLRC
nodes.summary: Parses timestamped LRC text into ordered lyric cues suitable for playback synchronization.

nodes.name: fetchLyrics
nodes.summary: Queries a lyrics service for a track and normalizes synchronized or plain-text responses.

nodes.name: ensure
nodes.summary: Ensures the lyric cache matches the active track while avoiding duplicate in-flight requests.

nodes.name: nowplaying.js

nodes.name: fetchArt
nodes.summary: Resolves embedded artwork for a track and stores a normalized data representation in the artwork cache.

nodes.name: lookupArtOnline
nodes.summary: Searches online metadata sources for missing artwork and reports the best usable image to the caller.

nodes.name: poll
nodes.summary: Reads the current playback provider and updates track, transport, and artwork state.

nodes.name: tick
nodes.summary: Schedules serialized playback polling and maintains timing information between provider updates.

nodes.name: sysmetrics.js
nodes.summary: Collects CPU, memory, disk, network, battery, temperature, and GPU metrics on independent polling cadences.

nodes.name: makeLoop
nodes.summary: Creates a guarded interval loop that prevents overlapping asynchronous metric polls.

nodes.name: pollFast
nodes.summary: Samples rapidly changing CPU, memory, and related system metrics.

nodes.name: pollMedium
nodes.summary: Samples medium-frequency disk, network, battery, and system status metrics.

nodes.name: pollSlow
nodes.summary: Refreshes slower-changing hardware and operating-system metadata.

nodes.summary: Detects whether NVIDIA telemetry is available and records the chosen GPU query path.

nodes.name: pollGpu
nodes.summary: Collects GPU load and temperature metrics using NVIDIA-specific or generic fallbacks.

nodes.name: getSnapshot
nodes.summary: Returns the latest grouped system metrics with freshness metadata for dashboard consumers.

nodes.name: providers.js
nodes.summary: Defines supported OAuth provider metadata and canonicalizes provider identifiers for Microsoft, GitHub, and Google integrations.

nodes.name: PRIVACY.md
nodes.summary: Explains open-quake's local-only data handling, including stored configuration, embedded third-party dashboards, USB device access, and the explicit absence of telemetry or audio capture.

nodes.name: PROJECT.md
nodes.summary: Defines the charter, accepted decisions, verification criteria, and implementation approach for automatically following the foreground Windows application without overriding manual panel navigation.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Introduces the DK-QUAKE driver and touchscreen launcher, surveys its grids, dashboards, bundled apps, hardware controls, theming, setup, licensing, and firmware safety constraints.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Begin with the project overview to understand open-quake as a Windows-first driver and touchscreen launcher for DK-QUAKE, ARIS-68, and Bedrock-style hardware. It introduces the grid, dashboard, app, knob, theming, licensing, and firmware-safety concerns that shape every layer explored later.

tour.title: Runtime and Packaging Contract
tour.description: The package manifest turns that product overview into an executable contract: Electron starts at app/main.js, native dependencies are rebuilt for Electron's ABI, and Windows artifacts are packaged and signed. Read it before the entry point so the runtime version, scripts, unpacked assets, and release targets are clear.
tour.languageLesson: In an Electron project, the package manifest describes both a Node.js application and a desktop distribution: the main field selects the privileged process entry point, while builder settings control artifact layout and native-file unpacking.

tour.title: Main Process Orchestration
tour.description: app/main.js is the architectural hub, coordinating configuration, windows, integrations, hardware, IPC, display placement, and lifecycle cleanup. Its unusually high fan-out provides the best map of how host-runtime responsibilities connect, while actionRunner.js illustrates how privileged Windows actions stay outside renderer code.

tour.title: Renderer Security Boundary
tour.description: Building on the main process, the two preload bridges expose small, purpose-specific APIs to the touchscreen and configuration renderers. The panel controller then implements grids, web dashboards, touch hit testing, knob navigation, and page selection without receiving unrestricted Node or IPC access.
tour.languageLesson: Electron's contextIsolation pattern places a preload script between an unprivileged renderer and the main process. A narrow contextBridge surface reduces the impact of renderer compromise by exposing capabilities instead of raw ipcRenderer access.

tour.title: Configuration Model and Editor
tour.description: The default configuration seeds pages and grids, while apps.json defines the bundled-app catalog and editor-facing option schemas. config.js and config.html turn those structures into the desktop editor for pages, groups, tiles, icons, integrations, and hardware settings, then send complete updates back across the guarded bridge introduced previously.

tour.title: Hardware Abstraction
tour.description: The multi-knob facade keeps the host runtime independent of a particular physical device. Behind it, the ARIS-68 connector handles the richer HID, touch, display, lighting, and firmware protocol, while the Bedrock connector supplies the same stable surface with compatible no-op display operations where necessary.
tour.languageLesson: CommonJS modules and EventEmitter-style device adapters make runtime substitution straightforward: callers depend on one behavioral interface even when the underlying hardware capabilities differ.

tour.title: Local Service Boundary
tour.description: sysserver.js is the bridge between hosted panel experiences and privileged application data, serving built-in pages, live metrics, app assets, app-local APIs, Office operations, and an outbound proxy. Its loopback binding, origin checks, path containment, response limits, and rotating capabilities are central design constraints for every served integration.

tour.title: OAuth and Secret Handling
tour.description: The authentication subsystem defines provider metadata, executes PKCE authorization and refresh flows, and persists tokens through the application's mutable configuration. secretStore.js and dpapi.js protect credentials at rest, while oauthConfigBoundary.js removes sensitive values before configuration reaches a renderer, completing the trust boundary established in Steps 4 and 7.

tour.title: Office Integration Flow
tour.description: The Office Graph service fixes the Microsoft provider and scopes in the main process, then normalizes profile, presence, and calendar results into a safe dashboard model. office.js consumes that model through a rotating capability, while the HTML and CSS provide a responsive touchscreen workspace with meeting focus, agenda, quick actions, and connection states.

tour.title: Native Windows Helpers
tour.description: Optional native helpers extend Electron into platform features that are awkward or unavailable through ordinary JavaScript APIs. reservedDisplay.js supervises the C# display-protection process, while the DPAPI binding and SMTC helpers provide credential encryption and media-session control with graceful degradation when toolchains or binaries are unavailable.
tour.languageLesson: The JavaScript-to-native boundary is intentionally process- or Node-API-based: structured streams support long-lived helpers, while a minimal native binding exposes narrowly scoped synchronous cryptographic operations.

tour.title: Extensible App Ecosystem
tour.description: Bundled pages demonstrate self-contained panel experiences, while the community catalog and drop-in skill explain how third-party apps extend the launcher. News Spotlight shows the full contract in practice: a manifest declares options and proxy policy, a renderer fetches and presents content, and an app-local server safely opens validated external links.

tour.title: Verification and Release
tour.description: Finish with focused tests that protect the highest-risk boundaries: encrypted secret persistence, OAuth capability isolation, and reserved-display process behavior. The build and signing hooks then compile first-party helpers, sign unpacked native artifacts, and produce trusted Windows releases, tying implementation invariants back to the packaging contract from Step 2.
